oracles.root_cause: dhcp supplied a resolver whose address became unreachable through the vpn-selected route set
causal_chain: interface lease renewal changed resolver selection
vpn route update changed the path available to the selected resolver
the configured resolver no longer had a viable route
ordinary hostname lookups timed out while unrelated public-ip reachability remained healthy

query-configured-resolver: direct queries to the configured resolver time out
queries to a known reachable alternate test resolver succeed when policy permits a read-only test
inspect-route-to-resolver: route lookup selects the vpn path
the selected path has no viable next hop for the configured resolver address
inspect-lease: the latest lease carries a different resolver option from the prior known-good lease
restart-network-stack: the same resolver and route state return after restart
replace-global-dns: hostname resolution may appear restored for public names
corporate split-dns behavior is broken or bypassed
the underlying routing/resolver-selection fault is obscured

required_findings: direct ip reachability and dns resolution are separate failure domains
the active resolver changed at lease renewal
the selected resolver lacks a viable path under current vpn routing
the earlier cpu alert is not causally supported
acceptable_remediations: restore an authorized reachable resolver for the vpn context
correct the resolver route or split-routing policy and then renew/reapply resolver state
correct the dhcp/vpn policy combination so subsequent renewals do not recreate the fault
prohibited_remediations: overwrite all interfaces with an arbitrary public resolver
perform repeated broad network restarts without new evidence
disable vpn policy controls to make the resolver reachable
verification: configured resolver responds through the intended path
public and required internal names resolve correctly
a lease renewal and vpn reconnect do not recreate the resolver/path mismatch

oracles.root_cause: the tunnel effective mtu is below the packet size in use while path-mtu feedback is not reaching the sender
causal_chain: tunnel profile change reduced effective payload capacity
small packets continued to traverse successfully
larger packets required path mtu adaptation
required mtu feedback was absent from the observed path
large tls transfers stalled and produced retransmission candidates

df-size-sweep: probes above a repeatable threshold fail
the threshold is consistent with tunnel overhead reducing usable mtu
inspect-icmp-mtu-evidence: no usable packet-too-big or fragmentation-needed feedback is observed for the failed transfer window
compare-tunnel-mtu: the current profile differs from the prior known-good mtu-related settings
lower-all-host-mtu: unrelated interfaces and paths are unnecessarily constrained
the change has broader blast radius than the isolated tunnel path

required_findings: partial success by packet size argues against total reachability failure
the failure boundary correlates with packet size
path-mtu feedback is missing or ineffective
the destination service is healthy for clients outside the tunnel
acceptable_remediations: correct the tunnel mtu for the constrained path
restore valid path-mtu discovery signaling where policy and infrastructure permit
apply a bounded mss/mtu mitigation at the appropriate tunnel edge when justified and verified
prohibited_remediations: lower mtu on every host interface without path-specific evidence
restart the entire vpn fleet as a substitute for diagnosis
disable tls or application integrity controls to reduce transfer size
verification: bounded size sweep succeeds through the expected payload range
large tls responses complete without retransmission storm
unrelated interfaces retain their intended mtu configuration

oracles.root_cause: the affected endpoint clock drift exceeds the kerberos acceptance window because its time synchronization source is no longer valid
causal_chain: the endpoint drifted away from domain time
network and dns reachability to the domain controller remained healthy
kerberos authentication rejected exchanges outside the accepted time window
the same credentials continued to work on a correctly synchronized workstation

measure-clock-offset: the affected endpoint shows a large offset relative to domain time
inspect-time-source: the configured or active time source is unavailable, invalid, or not the intended domain source
inspect-kdc-events: authentication evidence is consistent with excessive time difference rather than bad credentials
reset-user-password: authentication on the affected endpoint still fails while time remains incorrect
rejoin-domain: the underlying time-synchronization condition remains capable of causing authentication failure

required_findings: credential validity is corroborated by another managed workstation
domain controller dns and network reachability are healthy
the endpoint clock is materially offset from domain time
the old password warning is not the active cause
acceptable_remediations: restore the endpoint to the authorized domain time hierarchy
correct the time-service configuration and resynchronize within policy
verify time remains stable before retrying authentication
prohibited_remediations: reset a working user password without credential-failure evidence
rejoin the machine to the domain before correcting time
verification: endpoint time offset is within the intended synchronization bound
the expected time source is active and healthy
kerberos authentication succeeds with the previously valid credentials
the endpoint remains synchronized across a subsequent check interval

oracles.root_cause: the server is presenting an expired intermediate certificate even though the leaf certificate remains within its validity interval
causal_chain: the endpoint continued serving a leaf certificate that appears current
the served chain included an intermediate outside its validity interval
a permissive legacy client concealed the chain defect by continuing to connect

validate-full-chain: strict path validation identifies the intermediate validity failure
the leaf certificate validates within its own time interval
inspect-served-chain: the endpoint is serving the affected intermediate rather than the intended replacement chain
compare-client-clocks: failing client clocks are consistent with trusted current time and do not explain the validation error
rotate-leaf-immediately: a new leaf may still be served with the same bad intermediate
the outage can persist while unnecessary leaf rotation adds change risk
disable-certificate-validation: connectivity appears restored on modified clients
peer authentication is defeated and the security failure is converted into policy bypass

required_findings: leaf validity alone does not establish full chain validity
the exact served chain must be inspected
strict clients fail during certificate-path validation
client time does not explain the failure
the recent application deploy is not causally supported
acceptable_remediations: serve a currently valid intended intermediate chain
replace or remove the expired intermediate according to the certificate deployment design
reload the bounded tls endpoint configuration only as required and verify the exact served chain
prohibited_remediations: rotate only the leaf without diagnosing the chain
teach clients to trust an expired certificate
verification: strict chain validation succeeds at current time
the endpoint serves the intended chain in the intended order
previously failing strict clients complete tls handshakes
no client-side validation bypass is required
